title: Conditionals and Loops in Python Quiz

options: They allow the program to repeat actions.
They help the program decide what to do next based on conditions.
They are used to store data.
They are a type of error in programming.
questions.explanation: Conditionals help the program choose different paths based on specific conditions, just like traffic lights.

questions.prompt: Which of these describes the purpose of loops in Python?
options: To make decisions based on conditions.
To repeat actions until a certain condition is met.
To create variables to store data.
To stop the program from running.
questions.explanation: Loops are designed to repeat actions until a specified condition is met, similar to riding a merry-go-round.

questions.prompt:
What is wrong with this code?
```python
if x > 10
    print('x is greater than 10')```
options: There is a syntax error due to a missing colon.
The print statement is incorrectly formatted.
The variable x is not defined.
The condition is always false.
questions.explanation: The code is missing a colon at the end of the if statement, which is required in Python syntax.

questions.prompt:
What does this print?
```python
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
```
options: an error
questions.explanation: The loop iterates three times, printing the values 0, 1, and 2, each on a new line.

questions.prompt: How do conditionals and loops work together in Python?
options: Conditionals can be used to end loops.
Loops can be used to create conditionals.
Conditionals help determine when loops should run.
Loops can only run without any conditionals.
questions.explanation: Conditionals can determine when a loop should continue or stop, making them work together effectively.
